course_description:
Dental Practice II will allow students to consolidate their developing skills in intra-coronal restoration and enhance competence in history taking, diagnosis, care planning and management for dental patients with medical conditions. Students will develop an emerging understanding of the effects of common medical conditions on routine dental procedures. At the completion of this course, students will apply knowledge of head and neck anatomy, neurophysiology and pharmacology of local anaesthetic agents to deliver effective pain relief for restorative treatments.

This course follows on from DENT2060 and continues using simulated learning environments including pre-clinical laboratories to provide students with the opportunity to attain competency in the clinical skills required to provide preventive dental care and simple dental restorations. Students will also develop their clinical skills in a clinical environment and apply knowledge of oral diseases to explain clinical observations and to solve clinical problems.

Each week, students will have 4-hrs of preclinical lab sessions and 3-hrs of clinical work-related sessions. This will be supplemented with 3-hours of workshop sessions.

course_aims: The Dental Practice IIB course aims to consolidate students skills in intra-coronal restoration and develop an emerging understanding of the effects of common medical conditions on routine dental procedures.

learning_outcomes.description: Achieve manual dexterity skills appropriate for multi-surface intra-coronal restorations.
Conduct and record a thorough patient interview and clinical examination of the oral cavity and associated structures.
Explain the importance of person-centred practices for the provision of effective healthcare.
Create evidence-based and tailored preventive management plans for common dental diseases.
Apply understanding of head and neck anatomy, oral biology and oral histology to the effective management of pain and delivery of local anaesthetic agents.
Develop self-reflexivity in a simulated clinical context with patients from diverse social and cultural backgrounds.

assessment_details.task_description: The purpose of this assessment is to evaluate the student’s pre-clinical/peer clinic performance at the interim stage and provide formative feedback to support improvement before the final clinical competence assessment at the end of semester. Course Coordinator in consultation with the pre-clinical/peer clinic supervisory team will complete a report based on student’s clinical performance during the assessment period and quality of critical self-reflections following each session. See Submission Guidelines for all components that must be submitted for the interim clinical practice performance task to be assessed. Detailed assessment criteria and rubrics will be provided on Blackboard. Two domains will be assessed to an expectations met (EM) or not met (ENM) standard and mapped to the Professional competency requirements for the accreditation body for this program - The Australian Dental Council (Professional Competencies of the newly Qualified Dentist) The domains being assessed are: 1. Professionalism, Communication and Health Promotion 2. Clinical Treatment and Evaluation To achieve a pass, the criteria are as follows: All domains are weighted equally, and the student must achieve a pass in each domain, and an overall pass. A pass in each domain will involve a student receiving 3 or fewer "expectations not met" (ENM) mark in Domain 1, and no more than 3 "expectation not met" (ENM) in Domains 2. An overall pass for the report will involve a student receiving 6 or fewer "expectations not met" (ENM) mark across the 2 domains. Please note: Written feedback will be provided for any areas to improve as this is formative. Students must reflect on feedback and demonstrate improvement in the latter half of the semester. Logbooks may be randomly audited by the Course Coordinator for authenticity and supervisor signatures. Any significant peer-clinical concerns related to safety will be escalated immediately via course coordinator pathways and documented and taken into consideration for the assessment outcomes. There is no resubmission or resit available for this component. This is a formative assessment to enable the student to receive feedback on their developing clinical competency. Any significant clinical concerns pertaining to patient safety will be escalated via clinical communication pathways to the course coordinator and recorded on this report to be considered for the assessment outcome. assessment_details.title: Viva voce
assessment_details.task_description: The 15-minute examination with two examiners will assess each student's knowledge, understanding and ability in general dentistry at a level appropriate for end of year 2 BDSc(Hons). This assessment task will assess at the appropriate level, each student's knowledge, understanding, and ability in general dentistry including basic patient assessment and examination, range of diagnostic tests, rationale for early clinical decision making, basic care planning and sequencing treatment, rationale for treatment of dental caries, non-carious tooth surface loss, early pre and peer clinical skills including choice of materials, patient management, ethics and professionalism. All concepts learnt in preclinic, peer clinical sessions, workshops and seminars in Semester 2 mapped to course learning outcomes, will be examined. Students can expect to answer questions, draw and explain diagrams / models, perform short practical tasks and demonstrate concepts by role-playing. All aspects explored in Semester 2 may be examined. This not a MUST PASS assessment. The submitted portfolio must be COMPLETE in all the following respects and submitted by the published due date which will then be assessed as part of this assessment task. Any incomplete or missing information can result in a fail grade in this must pass assessment task.
Students must complete the portfolio for all pre-clinical/peer clinic and observational sessions. If no feedback (written or verbal) is provided by the supervisor during a session, the student must proactively seek feedback immediately after the session. The student should then record all feedback in the comments section and obtain the supervisor’s sign-off to confirm the discussion. A structured reflection for each session must be written around a specific task during the week, particularly where the supervisor/s have provided constructive feedback, or a grade of expectations not met was received.
